findings.title: New installations can bypass the GitHub-user verification when the webhook record is not present
findings.body: When no `Integration` row exists yet, this returns `pipeline.next_step()` before checking `github_authenticated_user` against an installer identity. The identity used by the later check is populated asynchronously from the GitHub installation webhook, so a user can complete the setup callback before that webhook has created the row (or when webhook delivery failed) and link an arbitrary known installation ID to their Sentry organization. This is precisely the path where the proposed authorization check is unavailable; the flow should wait for/require a verified installation sender record rather than treating a missing record as safe.

findings.title: Existing integrations without webhook sender metadata cause a server error
findings.body: `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` assumes every active existing GitHub integration has a sender object. Integrations created through the previous setup flow did not populate this metadata (and the normal setup test's expected metadata has no `sender`), so if such an integration has no OrganizationIntegration—for example after uninstalling and attempting to install it into another organization—this raises `KeyError` and returns a 500 instead of the installation failure response. Handle missing or malformed legacy metadata explicitly, ideally by rejecting it safely or obtaining a verified sender.
